claims.claim: The friction surrounding data centers centers heavily on electricity rather than public relations framing.

claims.claim: Most AI data centers being constructed across the country operate differently from traditional facilities tied directly to local grids.
claims.bestSource: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity
claims.evidence: The overwhelming majority of AI data centers being built elsewhere in the country are not designed this way. More than 160 new AI data centers have popped up across the U.S. in the past three years—a 70% increase from the last three year period, according to a Bloomberg News analysis . The notion of data center companies’ bringing their own power might seem attractive at first, because they wouldn’t be straining the grid.

editorial.claim: One perspective contends that the backlash is not fundamentally about electricity or water usage, pointing out that research suggests data centers can actually help lower electricity prices as higher demand drives increased energy production.

In Texas, Governor Greg Abbott transitioned from participating in ribbon-cutting ceremonies for major data centers to issuing explicit demands regarding their power usage, site selection, and overall economic contributions.Governments are already requiring the industry to generate its own electricity, and policymakers are even pushing data centers to provide a net increase in power.
